question: On brain-native questions about one synthetic company (meeting prep, who knows a topic, what changed at a company since a date), asked by a member in a DM or a room, does QM's brain tool (K1, T vs R) and its turn card (K2, TC vs T) improve the mean task score, and does the brain stack beat the same authorized knowledge as sandbox files (TC vs F, the headline), per frontier model (Opus 5.5, GPT-6.1 Sol), Holm-corrected across those six comparisons, with zero leaks in every arm, an unanswerable-control harm guard, and cost, token and latency margins. particle-1 is a labelled low-cost primary and carries no verdict alone. Design stage: this is design.json, not a runnable prereg.json; the pilot preregistration amendment adds pins and a prereg.json with the pilot cells, and the main preregistration adds the held-out block, n and the cap from the frozen rules.

arms.F: the audience manifest as files in the scope's sandbox workspace (notes/), read trace; no gbrain
arms.R: per-turn recall from the bound brain; K1a and K2a switches off; brain skill archived
arms.T: R plus the K1a brain tool, its prompt line and seeded skill; card off
arms.TC: T plus the K2a turn card
arms.N: no corpus, no binding, no files; brain skill archived

guard.fails_when: point drop over 10 points and the 95% interval excludes zero

heldout.used: n from the task-count rule, floor(n/3) per family, remainder to prep then who, in sealed order

power.sd_definition: pooled sd of per-task paired differences over the six confirmatory comparisons in the pilot, two repeats; 80% upper bound recorded

drop_order: N on frontier models to half the tasks

heldout_custody.block: added in the main preregistration PR
